subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should Mattermost native slash command registration fail closed for any non-HTTPS callback URL, including explicit HTTP configs, before this PR can merge?
rationale: The patch reduces cleartext exposure for reusable Mattermost slash-command tokens, but it intentionally breaks existing HTTP callback deployments until operators configure HTTPS.

options.title: Accept HTTPS-only after proof
options.body: Require redacted live Mattermost proof, resolve the branch conflict, refresh the PR body, and then land the fail-closed HTTPS-only policy.

options.title: Stage compatibility instead
options.body: Ask for a maintainer-designed deprecation or opt-in strict-mode path if preserving existing HTTP callback deployments matters more than immediate fail-closed hardening.

options.title: Reject this direction
options.body: Close or pause the PR if maintainers decide current warning-only HTTP callback behavior remains an accepted deployment mode.

recommendation.title: Accept HTTPS-only after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted live Mattermost proof, resolve the branch conflict, refresh the PR body, and then land the fail-closed HTTPS-only policy.

likelyOwner.reason: He moved this behavior into the current monitor-slash helper and is the strongest current-main routing signal for the runtime touchpoint.
